units.title: Paediatric Hip: Lines & Angles
units.guide: Two landmarks guard the child's hip: Shenton's line, arcing from the inferior margin of the superior pubic ramus to the medial head and neck - any pathology breaks it; and the neck-shaft angle, normal 130-135 degrees in adults, whose increase spells coxa valga and decrease coxa vara. The proximal femur carries a growth plate, its capital epiphysis being the head of the femoral epiphysis.

units.title: Coxa Vara
units.guide: Injure the growth plate of the femoral head and the trochanter keeps growing while head and neck stop: the angle drops and coxa vara is born. It comes in infantile/primary and acquired/secondary forms (Perthes, SCFE), and the clinic tells the tale - Trendelenburg gait from failed abduction, obligate external rotation on flexion, limited abduction and internal rotation, and a shortened limb.

units.title: Congenital Coxa Vara
units.guide: Congenital coxa vara traces back to damage of Fairbank's triangle, the vulnerable patch of the femoral neck. Do not confuse it: Babcock's triangle belongs to TB.

units.title: SCFE
units.guide: In SCFE the head stays home in the acetabulum while the neck slips - a Type I Salter-Harris fracture of the growth plate. It strikes boys at puberty (13-17 vs 11-14 for girls), overweight children, is idiopathic most often, and follows sex-hormone imbalance - hypothyroidism, hypogonadism, raised GH - which pushes bilaterality from 40% to 60%. Trethowan's line betrays it on the film: no longer cutting the head. Fix it: closed reduction, internal fixation, in situ pinning.

units.title: Osteochondritis
units.guide: Osteochondrosis is a self-limiting, childhood, necrotic wobble of the epiphyseal ossification centres, sparked by a primary vascular event or repetitive trauma. Perthes (femoral epiphysis) is the m/c, then Kohler's (navicular), Freiberg's (lunate), Panner's (capitulum - elbow pain), Osgood-Schlatter (tibial tuberosity) and Sever's (calcaneal epiphysis).

units.title: Perthes: Blood Supply
units.guide: Perthes - coxa plana, Legg-Calve-Perthes, Chandler's disease when it hits adults - is idiopathic spontaneous osteonecrosis. The femoral head drinks from two fountains: foveolar flow before 4, metaphyseal flow after 10; between 4 and 10 the supply shifts and the head stands exposed, so any insult lands as osteonecrosis.

units.title: Perthes: Features & Treatment
units.guide: Idiopathic and male, with protein S deficiency as its m/c association, 10-15% bilateral and a poor prognosis beyond age 6. It limps painlessly at first, pain later marching to the knee and groin, abduction and internal rotation stiff with obligate external rotors. MRI is the IOC (X-ray only shows late change); treatment sustains the head till vascularity resumes - no weight bearing, skin traction, Petrie/broomstick cast - and THA waits for skeletal maturity.

units.title: DDH: Basics & Epidemiology
units.guide: Once called congenital dislocation of the hip, DDH is idiopathic spontaneous subluxation of the femoral head from a flat, convex, shallow acetabulum - the head parked outside in utero. One in 1000 live births, girls over boys, left over right, 10% bilateral, favouring the first born breech female with a strong family history; Caucasians exceed Asians, perhaps because of how babies are carried.

units.title: DDH: Clinical Diagnosis
units.guide: Short limb, asymmetric thigh and gluteal folds, and Narath's absent femoral pulse against a present popliteal pulse under 3 months set the stage. Barlow (BAD) adducts and dislocates; Ortolani abducts and reduces the dislocated hip; Allis/Galeazzi finds the low knee in unilateral disease, and the Hilisic test speaks for bilateral DDH; the gait waddles and Trendelenburgs.

units.title: DDH: Investigations & Lines
units.guide: USG screens before 6 months; MRI confirms and plans. The child's acetabulum is triradiate cartilage of ilium, ischium and pubis, mapped by Hilgenreiner's line across its centres and Perkins' perpendicular off its lateral edge: the normal head sits in the inner, outer quadrant, the dysplastic head in the upper, outer.

units.title: DDH: Age-Wise Treatment
units.guide: The treatment clock: 0-6 months the Pavlik harness or von Rosen splint; 6-18 months open or closed reduction via Smith-Peterson approach; 18-36 months femoral osteotomy; beyond 3 years VDRO plus pelvic osteotomy (Salter, Pemberton); and past 10 years, total hip replacement after skeletal maturity.
